standard_prerequisites: Context span 4368-4377: F(T) = the set of families (f_1, f_2, ...) of morphisms f_i: T -> P^1; P^1 satisfies the sheaf property for fpqc coverings (Descent, fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms) and products of sheaves are sheaves, so F is an fpqc sheaf; the diagonal is representable since T x_F S is the scheme-theoretic intersection of the closed subschemes T x_{f_i, P^1, g_i} S inside T x S

Context span 4377-4390: SL_2 -> P^1 is surjective smooth affine; U = (SL_2)^infinity with the product morphism U -> F is an affine scheme; for f: T -> F the fibre Z = T x_F U is the infinite fibre product of the schemes Z_i = T x_{f_i, P^1} SL_2 over T; each Z_i -> T is surjective smooth affine, whence Z is a scheme flat and affine over T; a simple limit argument shows Z -> T is open, so U -> F is flat, surjective, and universally open

Context span 4392-4405: if F were an algebraic space it would be quasi-compact and separated (by the fibre-product description), so quasi-coherent cohomology would vanish above a cutoff (Cohomology of Spaces, vanishing proposition); but pulling back O(-2, -2, ...) under the projection (P^1)^infinity -> (P^1)^n, which has a section, gives a quasi-coherent sheaf with nonzero cohomology in degree n - a contradiction
core_obligations: F is an fpqc sheaf with representable diagonal (context)
U = (SL_2)^infinity -> F is a surjective, flat, universally open morphism from an affine scheme, in particular quasi-compact (context fibre-product analysis)
F is not an algebraic space: the context cohomology obstruction (nonvanishing H^n against the vanishing cutoff) rules it out
proof_roadmap: Verify the sheaf and diagonal properties from the context displays
Run the context fibre-product argument for the cover U -> F
Conclude with the context cohomology contradiction
